evidence.note: Authentication record declares only an Aad block (AuthorizationUri and Resource). No anonymous, key, or other kind is declared.
Data is fetched with Web.Contents against the Azure Resource Manager Resource Graph endpoint.
subscription and managementGroup are resources inside the tenant and map to database-or-resource-id.
optional options record of connector settings.
query text is passed as its own parameter, so it is other.
scope selects Tenant, Subscription, or Management group. No listed id fits a scope selector, so it is other.

options-fields.text: The options record accepts one field, resultTruncated (logical, AllowedValues true and false). When it is absent, GetPage defaults resultTruncated to true (line 73). When true, the request is not paged: nextSkipToken is forced to null (line 78), so only one page is fetched and no skip token is used.

evidence.note: Declares the resultTruncated field inside options.
Defaults resultTruncated to true when the option is missing.
When resultTruncated is true, nextSkipToken is null, which stops paging.
Next page token is read from Value.Metadata(previous)[SkipToken].
The token is sent as the $skipToken option in the request body.
Reads the $skipToken field from the response body.
Pages are produced by calling Table.GenerateByPage.
Local helper that builds pages with List.Generate. The connector itself does not call List.Generate to fetch pages (the List.Generate in Value.WaitFor is retry logic).

paging-stop.text: Paging stops when the response has no $skipToken, since Value.Metadata(previous)[SkipToken] is then null and ARGImpl returns null. It also stops when resultTruncated is true, because nextSkipToken is forced to null. The helper stops when getNextPage returns null.

evidence.note: nextToken is null when there is no skip token, so page is null.
nextSkipToken is null when resultTruncated is true, otherwise it comes from the body.
List.Generate stops when the page is null.
The response body is parsed with Json.Document.
The data array from the JSON body is converted to a table with Table.FromList.
Column names come from Record.FieldNames of the first returned row. No M types are assigned to them.
The type is copied from the first page's data (Value.Type), not declared by the connector.
ManualStatusHandling = {500, 400} is set on the Web.Contents call.
The status code is inspected and an error message is built from the error body.
Errors are raised with error from the response content.
Value.WaitFor retries the request with a delay.

retry-rule.text: Only HTTP 500 is retried. HTTP 400 is returned as an error immediately, and any other status is returned as a success. There are at most 3 attempts (Value.WaitFor count of 3, and a status-500 error only after iteration 3). The delay before each retry is 2 to the power of the iteration index, which is 1, 2, and 4 seconds (Number.Power(2, iteration)).

evidence.note: Status 500 returns null (retry) until iteration reaches 3, status 400 returns an error.
Delay is #duration(0,0,0,Number.Power(2, iteration)) with a count of 3.
Documentation.Name and LongDescription and Examples on the function type.
Documentation.FieldCaption and FieldDescription on parameters.
Documentation.SampleValues for query.
Documentation.AllowedValues for scope.
AzureResourceGraph.Query returns one table directly, with no navigation table.
TestConnection names AzureResourceGraph.Query with the query resources | limit 1.
No Table.View, OnNativeQuery, or folding handler exists. The query is sent through Web.Contents as a plain string.
The connector is one .pq file.
Extension.LoadString is used for localized text.
Icon PNGs are loaded with Extension.Contents.
